label: Allocation under predicted costs
summary: A runnable reference for allocation, routing and scheduling from predicted costs: greedy assignment, optimal assignment on predictions and optimal assignment with an uncertainty penalty, compared on realised cost and on how optimistic the promise was.
runtime: Python 3.11+ with numpy, pandas, scikit-learn, scipy and pytest (about 1 second)
run: python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate && pip install -r requirements.txt
expected: make_data.py prints 150 instances of a 30 by 30 assignment problem. baseline.py reports realised cost 128.9 for greedy (40% above the oracle), 115.0 for the optimal assignment on predictions (25% above; it promised 77.1, an optimism gap of 49%), and 109.5 with an uncertainty penalty (19% above); the oracle with true costs is 92.0. pytest reports 5 passed.

files.purpose: Square assignment instances with true costs, noisy predictions and per-pairing uncertainty
Greedy, optimal and uncertainty-penalised assignment, realised cost, optimism gap and regret against the oracle
Executable gates: determinism, valid assignments, optimality on a known example, winner's curse and the penalty

synthetic.description: 150 instances of a 30 by 30 assignment problem with log-normal true costs and predicted costs that carry multiplicative noise whose size differs by pairing.
knobs: n_instances, n: number and size of the instances
seed: identical seed gives an identical set

slots.meaning: model estimate of the cost of each task-resource pairing
capacity, time windows and compatibility the plan must satisfy
what the plan said it would cost against what it cost
how much the plan changes between re-solves

data.threshold: pytest -k deterministic passes; median prediction error between 0.1 and 0.5 on the log scale
data.how: Run pytest in the kit directory

features.threshold: Every assignment is a permutation of the 30 resources, the optimiser never loses to greedy on the costs it is given, and a 3 by 3 example is solved to its optimum of 4.0

baseline.metric: Greedy and optimal regret and optimism
baseline.threshold: Optimal assignment on predictions has an optimism gap of at least 30% and lower regret than greedy (the kit: 49% and 25% against 40%)

challenger.threshold: At least 3 points of regret lower than the optimal assignment on raw predictions (the kit: 19% against 25%)

tests.pass: Every plan uses each resource once and the optimiser's total on predictions never exceeds greedy's
A 3 by 3 example is solved to its known optimum of 4.0
Optimism gap of at least 30%, and an honest promise (under 10%) with true costs
The optimiser beats greedy by 5 points and the penalty gains another 3

lessons.evidence: The optimal assignment on predictions promised 77.1 and realised 115.0: the optimiser picked the pairings whose errors happened to be optimistic.
Adding a premium for uncertain pairings cuts regret from 25% to 19% against the oracle.

lessons.trap: A greedy plan because it is simple
lessons.evidence: Greedy assignment realises 128.9, 40% above the oracle, against 115.0 for the optimal assignment.

lessons.trap: Measuring plan quality on the planning data
lessons.evidence: Costs are judged on realised (true) costs, never on the predictions the plan was built from.

target: The quantity to minimise is realised total cost. Predictions are inputs only; the plan is scored against true costs, and the oracle (the optimal plan under true costs) is the reference.

headline.challenger: optimal assignment with an uncertainty penalty, realised cost 109.5
